tagline: Up the canal and the lake, fort by fort, to Canada.
intro: Out of Waterford the passage takes US 4 north up the Hudson beside the Champlain Canal and its eleven locks, numbered 1 to 12. There is no lock 10. At Whitehall the canal reaches Lake Champlain, and from there the road keeps to the lake's west shore, by NY 22, US 9 and NY 9B, all the way to Rouses Point.

This was the water road between the Hudson valley and the St. Lawrence, and it was guarded accordingly. Forts went up at Ticonderoga and at Crown Point, fifteen miles apart, about a day's travel in their time.

moments.title: Whitehall
moments.text: Here Benedict Arnold built a fleet to meet the British at Valcour Island, and in 1960 the state legislature declared the town the birthplace of the United States Navy.

moments.title: Fort Ticonderoga
moments.text: A French star fort at the narrows, named from a Mohawk word for the junction of two waterways, taken from the British by Ethan Allen and Benedict Arnold in May 1775.

moments.title: Rouses Point
moments.text: The first fort here was mistakenly built on the Canadian side of the line and is sometimes called Fort Blunder. Some of its stone built a church, now a family home.
